name: MCP for Research Software
outcome: Expose research software functionality through an MCP interface.
description: Expose a scientific Python function through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Connect a supplied compatible client, inspect requests, validate results and restrict permissions. Direct model tool calling (A03) is recommended for application developers, but not required to build a server.
external: Basic Python, command-line use, Git, package environments and basic client–server concepts. Familiarity with AI tool use in an existing client.
prior: Basic generative AI literacy and familiarity with model-driven tool use
Basic Python, Git and terminal use
Ability to operate an MCP-capable client (guided setup supplied)
learn: Expose a scientific function through a typed MCP interface
Connect an existing compatible client and inspect calls
Test input validation, failure handling and access boundaries
tools: Claude Code CLI or Codex CLI (choose one)
modules: Connecting a client and observing calls
moduleDescriptions: Distinguish hosts, clients and servers; identify permitted capabilities.
Wrap a climate-data function with a typed interface and bounded inputs.
Connect an existing client and inspect tool requests and results.
Test invalid input and unavailable services; restrict access and record versions.
practice: Wrap the existing SSC climate-data script as an MCP tool and call it from a supplied client.
acceptance: Valid input returns the expected result; malformed input is rejected; unintended file or network access is not allowed.
prerequisiteRationale: A03 is recommended for understanding model-directed tools; a supplied MCP client makes direct API tool calling unnecessary.
